title: Learning Efficient Guardrails for Compliance
claim: Agents can finish a task yet break explicit and cumulative policies that conventional safety checks miss; a policy-aware guardrail catches them.
layout: Stacked boxes: instruction, policy, agent actions, then guardrail verdicts; icon-labeled tabs
description: A worked example of a web agent ordering food for an office birthday party. The top-left purple box gives the instruction. Below it, a blue box lists four policies, each with an icon: no alcohol, at most one cake, budget of $200 or less, and include vegan food. A large green box at right lists six agent actions with food icons and a robot at the top. Actions 3 (champagne) and 5 (cupcake pack) are bold, and the checkout total of $227.95 is in red. At bottom left, a brown 'Traditional Guardrails' box says no safety risks were detected. At bottom right, a red-outlined 'Policy Violation!' box lists alcohol included, more than one cake, and budget exceeded. A barrier icon labeled 'Policy Guardrail' sits beside it. Dashed rounded boxes with colored tabs separate each component.
caption: Example trajectory illustrating agent actions, policies, and violations. The agent completes the task but violates policies both directly (alcohol) and cumulatively (more than one cake, total cost > $200), cases that traditional guardrails fail to detect.
abstract: Autonomous web agents are increasingly deployed for long-horizon tasks, yet their ability to adhere to real-world policies remains critically underexplored compared to standard safety objectives. To address this gap, we introduce PolicyGuardBench, a benchmark of 60k policy-trajectory pairs designed to evaluate compliance through both full-trajectory and novel prefix-based violation detection tasks. Using this dataset, we train PolicyGuard, a lightweight guardrail model that achieves strong detection accuracy while maintaining high inference efficiency. Notably, our model demonstrates robust generalization capabilities, preserving high performance even on unseen domains. These contributions establish a comprehensive framework for studying policy compliance, showing that accurate and generalizable guardrails are feasible at small scales.
